limits: One live time-map draft per application data directory, one host-owned Service; concurrent independent Services bypassing the host lock are outside the contract.
Version 1 only, 4 MiB payload/8 MiB file/100000 rows per map/128 bytes per table string; limits do not establish large-form usability or performance.
Only already confirmed checkpoints are recoverable after reload/restart. Unconfirmed final input can be lost after force termination; no zero-loss-at-any-instant claim.
No new real native Wails window/OS Quit, process-kill, power-loss, disk exhaustion, sync/rename hardware fault or cross-platform filesystem acceptance.
Velocity, playback parameters, ordinary numeric fields, settings/conversation drafts and pointer previews are outside this recovery increment.
No database/schema/dependency or Agent/CLI/IPC capability change; no music auto-apply or operation replay, model/audio/physical device/clean-install acceptance.
developmentFindings: Browser test transport initially did not whitelist the three new real service methods; added only those methods to the test bridge.
An initial browser wait converted an unawaited Promise to true before the file contained a payload; corrected to await the actual persisted condition.

An existing page-reload transition produced a CDP 'Inspected target navigated or closed' error; polling now retries only known transient navigation/context-destruction errors, retaining application exceptions as failures.
The new clear protocol retains an empty-payload token barrier to prevent delayed initial saves from reappearing. No old-format reader or migration was added.
